meta.note: Anonymized public copy. Buyer leads were real companies found in public channels; names, contacts and URLs are removed here out of respect for them. Seller products are fictional test fixtures. Total = Fit*2 + Contact + Timing (max 14).

scenarios.finding: Launch dates are public and founders are named — timing signals are the strongest of any segment. But 0 of 3 had a published email, and launch-day outreach is already late for a first video; the list must be run continuously against upcoming launches.
scenarios.segment: Products launching now / next (Product Hunt, BetaList, crowdfunding)
scenarios.seller_product: LaunchClip — launch-video SaaS for products going to market ($99/video, fictional)

leads.why_now: Launched on Product Hunt today; iOS app still in App Store review = next launch imminent; serial maker who ships several apps a year
Pre-launch post yesterday, officially launched on PH today; founder personally answering community questions
Launched on PH yesterday; B2B SaaS selling to creators with ongoing video needs

scenarios.finding: Pain evidence is unusually rich and self-scoring (incumbent price hikes created dated, specific complaint posts). Two traps: 5 of 12 raw candidates were competitors' content marketing in disguise, and real pain posts decay within weeks — authors DIY a cron fix fast.
scenarios.segment: Indie developers & small SaaS teams unhappy with incumbent monitoring tools
scenarios.seller_product: Pingtail — lightweight uptime monitoring SaaS ($9/mo, fictional)

leads.why_now: PH launch today across web/Android/Chrome; iPhone app in review — biggest traffic spike still ahead, lots of surface to keep alive
Production app down up to 24h because Supabase free tier auto-paused; lost his biggest prospect; publicly wrote he would set up monitoring before next launch; runs multiple live apps
~1 month ago: monitor showed 100% while users saw 500s (DB outage masked by CDN cache); rewrote his checks, still on free-tier tooling

scenarios.finding: Competitor review sections are a self-supplying lead list: store name + date + pain in their own words, down to feature level. Counter-trap: the purest pain (community forums) is anonymous and unreachable, and review streams mix this month's complaints with 2021's — dates must be checked one by one.
scenarios.segment: Independent Shopify store owners publicly unhappy with returns apps
scenarios.seller_product: ReturnEase — self-serve returns portal for Shopify stores ($39/mo, fictional)

leads.why_now: Oct 2026 review: switched Loop -> AfterShip, upgraded to top tier, exchanges and store-credit returns still broken after 3 weeks of backend runaround — a live second-switch window
Jun 2026 public complaint: '30-minute setup' took hours; automation broken on lower tiers (carrier not auto-selected, returns fail); discount promise reversed
After ~2 years on Loop, publicly complained in Nov 2025 that cancelling the account is 'nearly impossible' — clear exit intent, only contract-locked
Feb 2025: on Loop, returns vs exchanges indistinguishable and exchanges spawn duplicate orders polluting repeat-purchase metrics; kept being charged after cancelling
Dec 2025 complaint: weeks into Loop and still not configured; onboarding specialist replies slowly — a self-serve simple portal is the direct antidote

scenarios.finding: Opening press releases are the richest source: media-contact blocks name the owner and often print a real email (clinic websites hide behind forms). The tax: 'new clinic' search results are polluted by DSO chains (Aspen 1,100+ locations, LaserAway, mydentist) that must be filtered out one by one, and verified emails exist for only 3 of 12 deep-dived candidates.
scenarios.segment: Independent dental & aesthetic clinics (new openings + visible front-desk pain)
scenarios.seller_product: Remindly Clinic — appointment reminders & no-show backfill for independent dental/med spas ($49/mo, fictional)

leads.why_now: Relaunched Aug 2026 and building its patient book; long high-value bookings (implants, full-mouth reconstruction) are the most expensive chairs to leave empty
Opened Mar 2026; only open Mon-Thu, so chair time is scarcer than usual
Opened Sep 23, 2026 — under a month old, still in the schedule-shaping phase
Launched Oct 1, 2026: rotating clinic with deliberately scarce slots that book out — an unfilled cancellation cannot be backfilled ad hoc
Multiple WebMD reviews: phones ring unanswered all day, lines constantly busy — the front desk is demonstrably underwater
Reviews describe 55-minute in-room waits and front-desk chaos; the practice explicitly tells patients it does NOT notify a waitlist when slots open — the exact feature being sold
